Subject: Coffee chat request from an MBA candidate interested in renewable project finance

Hi Maria,

I'm Omar Haddad, an MBA candidate in the Class of 2028. Before school, I worked as an analyst at Greenfield Energy Partners from 2021 to 2026, modeling solar project returns. I'm now working toward a career in renewable project finance, and I'd really like to hear how you got into renewable energy finance and how your path led to your role as Managing Director at Solaris Capital.

Would you be open to a 20-minute coffee chat or call in the coming weeks? I'm happy to work around your schedule.

Thank you,
Omar Haddad
questions: How did you first get into renewable energy finance? Was it a deliberate move, or did it evolve from earlier work?
Which experiences or decisions mattered most in your progression to Managing Director at Solaris Capital?
From your seat as an MD, how well does a background modeling solar project returns translate into a project finance role, and what gaps would you expect someone like me to need to close?
How has your view of what makes a renewable energy investment attractive changed since you first entered the field?
If you were starting your path into renewable energy finance today from an MBA program, what would you prioritize or do differently?

tmay_1min.text: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me, Maria.
I'm Omar Haddad, and I'm an MBA candidate in the Class of 2028.
Before business school, I worked as an analyst at Greenfield Energy Partners from 2021 to 2026, where I modeled solar project returns.
That role gave me a disciplined view of how assumptions drive project economics.
Over those years, I became increasingly focused on renewable energy finance
, and my career goal is to work in renewable project finance.
I see the MBA as a way to broaden my perspective beyond modeling and to prepare for that next step.
I reached out because I'd like to learn how you got into renewable energy finance and how your path led to your role as Managing Director at Solaris Capital.
I'd value your perspective on what matters most when building a career in this field.

tmay_2min.text: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me, Maria. I appreciate it.
I'm Omar Haddad, an MBA candidate in the Class of 2028.
I'll share a bit about where I've been and where I'm hoping to go.
Before business school, I spent 2021 to 2026 as an analyst at Greenfield Energy Partners.
My core work there was modeling solar project returns.
That experience gave me a practical understanding of how the numbers behind a project shape the decisions around it, and it taught me to be rigorous about the assumptions that go into a model.
Working through those models also showed me how many parties have a stake in a single project's outcome.
It was also where I came to see renewable energy finance as the area I wanted to build my career in.
That's what brought me to the MBA.
My goal is to work in renewable project finance,
and I'm using this time to round out my perspective beyond modeling, to understand the broader business side of these deals, and to learn from people who have built careers in the field.
That's a big part of why I wanted to speak with you.
I'm interested in learning how you got into renewable energy finance
and how your path led to your role as Managing Director at Solaris Capital.

I'd especially value hearing which experiences shaped your thinking most along the way, and what you would focus on if you were in my position today, with a modeling background and a clear interest in project finance.
I'm grateful for any perspective you're willing to share.
